counterfactual_rationale: The linked bug is a GB200 DeepSeek V3.2 NVFP4 FlashInfer-MoE failure where q had the wrong dtype. A GB200/NVFP4 model smoke test in the hardware matrix could plausibly have exposed this before merge.

The PR fixes PPLX+CUTLASS MoE integration issues, including topk_ids dtype and a different CUTLASS MoE call signature. A DP/PPLX serving test using the CUTLASS MoE backend could plausibly have caught the failure.

The record explicitly says overlap mode hit illegal memory access and was fixed by introducing synchronization. A schedule/overlap stress test, possibly under memcheck, could plausibly have exposed the missing synchronization.

The failure appears only when a pinned offload region reaches the cudaHostRegister size ceiling around 512 GiB. An edge-size allocation test for very large offload regions could plausibly have caught the startup failure.

The PR fixes illegal memory access in blockwise CUTLASS FP8 GEMMs by keeping predicates and loaded values aligned. Running the failing GEMM shape under a memory checker could plausibly have flagged the invalid access.

The patch gates a fused MoE top-k kernel when experts per group exceed the kernel's MAX_VPT=32 limit, and the record shows a Kimi-VL crash through that path. A top-k edge test with larger expert-group counts could plausibly have caught the assertion/crash.

The record describes correcting a FlashInfer CUTLASS MoE tuning token bound to address suboptimal performance, and the validation is functional/performance benchmarking. I did not see evidence of wrong output, crash, hang, or severe availability failure.

The crash occurs when NVFP4 DeepEP high-throughput all2all selects a backend lacking dispatch_router_logits and raises NotImplementedError. A wide-EP NVFP4 serving test with that all2all backend could plausibly have caught the bad backend selection.
The linked issue reports V1 MLA failing to import get_flash_attn_version from the wrong path. A V1 MLA startup smoke test could plausibly have caught this import failure.

The PR changes ROCm rotary embedding selection because the Triton implementation was incompatible with torch.compile. A ROCm torch.compile matrix test for Qwen-VL rotary embeddings could plausibly have exposed it.

The CUTLASS MoE pre-reorder kernel overflowed int32 destination-offset arithmetic for large routed buffers, causing illegal access or wrong writes. A large-offset boundary test above 2^31 elements could plausibly have caught it.

The QuickReduce path converted large BF16 residuals to FP16, producing non-finite values for GPT-OSS activations above FP16 range. Tests with realistic or adversarial high-magnitude all-reduce inputs on ROCm could plausibly have exposed the corruption.

The patch removes an incorrect FA4 assertion and adds broad FA4 KV-cache unit coverage. A randomized FA4 wrapper test over optional rotary-related arguments and cache layouts could plausibly have caught the false assertion.
The record says an express-laned PR caused a CI break by failing to import AttentionType in attention backends. A normal backend import/startup test could plausibly have caught this before merge.

The NpuFuseEPMoE layer was missing initialization parameters, according to the PR motivation. An NPU EP-MoE initialization smoke test in hardware CI could plausibly have caught the missing-parameter failure.
The PR says a previous change broke ModelOpt NVFP4 MoE models and validates with NVFP4 MoE serving/evaluation. A Blackwell/NVFP4 MoE E2E test could plausibly have caught the breakage.
CPU inference entered a GPU-only JIT top-k path and failed during request processing. CPU hardware/back-end CI for MiniMax-M2 request handling could plausibly have exposed the bad dispatch.

The record shows DeepSeek V4 HiSparse accuracy improving from 0.825 to 0.960 with the compressor_v2 fix. A realistic model-accuracy workload for the HiSparse compressor path could plausibly have exposed the degradation.
The TRT-LLM NVFP4 DP/EP path crashed on an assertion that moe_quant_config was None. A DP/EP NVFP4 serving/evaluation configuration like the one in the test plan could plausibly have caught it.

The RoPE cache was too short for EAGLE long-sequence/speculative positions, producing an illegal memory access. Edge tests with long positions and speculative decoding could plausibly have caught the out-of-bounds cache access.

The Triton MoE path mishandled -1 invalid/non-local topk_ids, misrouting slots and summing unwritten intermediate data. Unit tests with EP topk_ids containing -1 sentinels could plausibly have exposed the garbage outputs.

The PR is specifically for illegal memory in trtllm allreduce fusion and provides a serving reproducer. Running that fusion path under a dynamic memory checker could plausibly have flagged the invalid access.

The build failed on Hopper because cutlass_fp4_group_mm was registered even though its implementation was compiled only for SM100. A Hopper build/import matrix could plausibly have caught the undefined-symbol error.

The patch prevents FA3 forward_decode from enabling cascade attention unless spec_info is present, separating draft-decode from idle mode. A speculative decoding serving test that exercises idle and draft phases could plausibly have caught the bad mode handling.

The XPU kernel lacked the new topk_softplus_sqrt argument, so the workaround falls back to the old interface on XPU. An XPU kernel/API compatibility CI job could plausibly have exposed the argument mismatch.

The CPU split-KV scratchpad was undersized, allowing split outputs to overlap reduction flags and hang reduce_splits. A bounds-checked or sanitizer build on the CPU split-KV workload could plausibly have caught the overwrite before it manifested as a hang.

The assertion appears when Qwen3-Next has moe_intermediate_size 512 and TP=8, producing an intermediate size of 64 for flashinfer_trtllm. Shape tests over TP partitions and small intermediate sizes could plausibly have caught it.

The RMSNorm kernels changed reduction block size with num_tokens, so the same token produced different batch-invariant outputs across batch sizes. Batch-invariance tests that perturb surrounding batch size could plausibly have exposed the reduction-order difference.

The fp8 DeepGEMM path failed compilation because Dynamo could not trace platform capability helpers. A torch.compile inference test on affected FP8/DeepGEMM models could plausibly have caught the compilation failure.

The AMD skinny_gemm kernels could not handle non-contiguous tensors and could produce failures or inaccuracies. Tests that pass non-contiguous tensors through the ROCm wrapper could plausibly have caught the issue.
